senses.definition: One of four seasons, traditionally the second, marked by the longest and typically hottest days of the year due to the inclination of the Earth and thermal lag. Typically regarded as spanning either the period between the summer solstice to the autumnal equinox, or the months of June, July, and August in the Northern Hemisphere and the months of December, January and February in the Southern Hemisphere.
examples: Gradually, the end of summer hove into sight.
I'm going to the Gambia in the summer.

quotes.text: At twilight in the summer there is never anybody to fear—man, woman, or cat—in the chambers and at that hour the mice come out. They do not eat parchment or foolscap or red tape, but they eat the luncheon crumbs.

senses.definition: (poetic or humorous) year; used to give the age of a person, usually a young one.
examples: He was barely eighteen summers old.
She had seen not more than twenty summers.

senses.definition: (figuratively) Most flourishing, happy, or beautiful period; golden age, prime.

quotes.text:
O! craving heart, for the lost flowers
And sunshine of my summer hours!

senses.definition: (countable, fashion) Someone with light, pinkish skin that has a blue undertone, light hair and eyes, seen as best suited to certain colors of clothing.
(intransitive) To spend the summer, as in a particular place on holiday.

quotes.text: For he was an oddity, a black multimillionaire who summered on the Riviera, had an apartment in Paris and a penthouse, in a building he owned, high above Sugar Hill.

senses.definition: (architecture) A horizontal beam supporting a building.
